tour.name: Versailles Private Day Trip from Paris: Palace, Hall of Mirrors, Gardens & Trianon
tour.subtitle: A private day at the palace of the Sun King with a licensed guide and car: the State Apartments and the Hall of Mirrors at opening time, lunch in the gardens, the fountains, the Grand and Petit Trianon and Marie-Antoinette's hamlet.

tour.overview:
Louis XIV turned his father's hunting lodge at Versailles into the largest palace in Europe and, in 1682, moved the court and the government there from Paris. For more than a century, until the Revolution forced Louis XVI and Marie-Antoinette back to Paris in October 1789, Versailles was the centre of power and the model every European court tried to copy. The palace and park have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979.

This private day lets you see Versailles properly, which is impossible in a rushed half day. With a licensed guide, you enter the palace at opening time and walk through the State Apartments and the Hall of Mirrors before the crowds. After lunch, the car and a little train help you cover the vast estate: the formal gardens and fountains, the Grand Trianon, where the king escaped the court, and the Petit Trianon and hamlet, Marie-Antoinette's private world.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 8 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Paris
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy to moderate; about 7 km on gravel paths, with an electric cart or the little train to shorten distances

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Royal Chapel and the State Apartments.
• The Hall of Mirrors.
• The Queen's Apartments.
• The gardens, the Latona and Apollo fountains and the Grand Canal.
• The Grand Trianon and the Petit Trianon.
• The Queen's Hamlet.

WHY THIS WORKS
We arrive for the first entry of the day and leave the gardens and Trianon for the afternoon, when the crowds are in the palace, and we use the car to save the long walk across the park.

WHO IT SUITS
History lovers, families and anyone who wants to understand the France of the kings and the Revolution.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer castles in the countryside, choose our Loire Valley châteaux tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The palace is closed on Mondays. The musical fountain shows run on weekends and some weekdays from April to October and need an extra garden ticket on those days. The palace is very busy on Tuesdays and Sundays.

days.name: The palace of Versailles, the Hall of Mirrors, the gardens, the Trianon palaces and Marie-Antoinette's hamlet
days.description:
What to expect: the full estate of the kings of France in one day, with a licensed guide, private car, Passport tickets and lunch.

Your driver collects you at your hotel at about 8:00 for the 40-minute drive west to Versailles. Your guide meets you on the cobbled Royal Courtyard, under the gilded gate, for the first entry of the day. Inside, you see the Royal Chapel, where Louis XVI and Marie-Antoinette were married in 1770, and walk through the State Apartments, each dedicated to a planet and its god, from the Salon of Hercules to the Salon of Apollo, the throne room.

Then you enter the Hall of Mirrors, 73 metres long, with 357 mirrors facing seventeen windows that look over the gardens, and a painted ceiling celebrating the victories of Louis XIV. Here the German Empire was proclaimed in 1871 and the Treaty of Versailles was signed in 1919. You continue through the Queen's Apartments to her bedchamber, where royal babies were born in public and from which Marie-Antoinette escaped the mob in October 1789 by a hidden door.

After lunch in one of the restaurants of the gardens, you walk down the terraces designed by André Le Nôtre, past the Latona Fountain and the Apollo Fountain to the Grand Canal, 1.6 kilometres long, where the court once sailed gondolas sent from Venice. In season, music plays and the fountains are turned on as they were for Louis XIV. Your driver, or the little train, takes you across the park to the Grand Trianon, the pink marble palace the king built to escape court life, and the Petit Trianon, Marie-Antoinette's refuge. You finish at the Queen's Hamlet, a make-believe Normandy village with a mill, a dairy and a farm, built for her in the 1780s. You are back at your hotel at about 16:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:00 – Pick-up at your hotel in Paris.
09:00 – The palace: Royal Chapel, State Apartments, Hall of Mirrors, Queen's Apartments (about 2 hours).
11:15 – Gardens and terraces.
12:15 – Lunch in the gardens.
13:30 – Fountains and the Grand Canal.
14:15 – Grand Trianon and Petit Trianon.
15:15 – The Queen's Hamlet.
16:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The palace is closed on Mondays and on some public holidays.
• On musical fountain days the garden ticket is included in the Passport.
• Golf carts can be rented in the park for those who prefer not to walk.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, Passport ticket, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: golf cart or bicycle rental, drinks with lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Do we skip the lines?
faq.answer: We book timed Passport tickets for the first entry of the day, so you avoid the ticket queue. There is still a security check, which is fastest at opening time.

faq.question: On which days is the tour not possible?
faq.answer: The palace is closed on Mondays. Tuesdays and Sundays are the busiest days; we recommend Wednesday to Friday.

faq.question: Are the entrance tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes, the Passport ticket covering the palace, the gardens (including musical fountain days) and the Trianon estate.

faq.question: Is there much walking?
faq.answer: The estate is huge: about 7 km if you walk everything. Your driver and the little train cut this down, and golf carts can be rented.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, lunch at a restaurant in the gardens. Vegetarian, gluten-free and other diets can be arranged.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the secret door, the fountains and the farm animals at the hamlet. We keep the palace visit lively.

faq.question: Is it suitable for wheelchair users?
faq.answer: Largely. The palace has lifts and an accessible route, and wheelchairs can be borrowed. The garden paths are gravel; the car can reach the Trianon.

faq.question: Can we see the fountains working?
faq.answer: The musical fountain shows run on weekends and some weekdays from April to October. Tell us if this matters and we will choose a date accordingly.

faq.question: Can we bring a bag?
faq.answer: Small bags are fine. Large bags and suitcases are not allowed in the palace; you can leave them in the car.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes for the gravel paths, and a hat in summer: the gardens have little shade.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: April to October for the gardens and fountains in full glory. Winter is quiet inside the palace, but the fountains are off.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 72 hours before the tour, because palace tickets are non-refundable after that. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
